transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-07-07 16:00 UTC | Duration: 46m | Attendees: Sara Lin, Devon Park (Redwood) — Maya Ortiz, Jamal Peters, Leila Chen (BlueHarbor)

Auto-summary (auto-generated, may be partial): Discussed quickstart path (free credits), time-to-first-token, and whether to start with hosted API or size dedicated. BlueHarbor has regulatory concerns for a subset of PII workloads which may need a private VPC pilot or on-prem.

[00:00:00] Sara Lin: Hi everyone, thanks for joining — I'm Sara, account lead for Redwood Inference. Quick roll call?
[00:00:08] Maya Ortiz: Maya here, CTO at BlueHarbor. Jamal and Leila here as well.
[00:00:12] Jamal Peters: Jamal, platform.
[00:00:15] Leila Chen: Leila, ML.
[00:00:18] Sara Lin: Awesome, thanks. We planned to cover quickstart credits and expected time-to-first-token, plus run through hosted vs dedicated vs private. Devon from our SE team will cover perf/benchmarks. Devon, over to you.
[00:00:30] Devon Park: Hey everyone. Quick note — I might use a couple of shorthand names, like the runtime or KV cache. If anything is unclear, stop me.
[00:00:38] Maya Ortiz: Sure. We have about 3 main questions: how fast can we go from sign-up to a call for engineers, what are cost numbers for the steady state vs peak, and what privacy controls we get.
[00:00:48] Devon Park: Great. Time-to-first-token — our PLG path typically gets engineers from sign-up to first successful API call in under an hour, usually 15–30 minutes if you follow the quickstart. We give free credits for the pilot — for cases like yours we usually offer a 50k token credit to validate real prompts.
[00:01:05] Leila Chen: Is that the same for hosted and dedicated?
[00:01:08] Sara Lin: The credit is for hosted onboarding. Dedicated setup requires sizing and a contract — but we can do a short PoC using hosted accounts with a dedicated tenant-like environment, or a short reserve of capacity depending on timing.
[00:01:22] Jamal Peters: For the PII flows, we can't send raw customer IDs to outside-hosted services unless we have contractual controls. We'd need assurances — SOC2, KMS integration, and audit logs.
[00:01:33] Devon Park: Totally. We have SOC 2 Type II, SSO via SAML/Okta, RBAC at token and route level, and KMS options for encryption at rest for our Private offering. For hosted, we also offer per-tenant data deletion and short retention for logs; that can be tightened under an enterprise contract.
[00:01:49] Maya Ortiz: Can you run the KMS through our HSM? We need customer-managed keys.
[00:01:53] Devon Park: For Private (VPC or on-prem) yes—customer-managed KMS/HSM is supported. For Hosted we do offer KMS integrations but not full HSM custody unless it's part of a Private deployment. That's something we can map out.
[00:02:05] Leila Chen: From a perf perspective we need <120ms p95 for single-turn scoring at 16 tokens average, and we have bursts to 200 qps for some endpoints. How realistic is that on hosted?
[00:02:18] Devon Park: On hosted with high-tier service we can route to low-latency pools, p95 numbers depend on model size and batching. For 16-token single-turn scoring, smaller quantized models can hit sub-100ms p95 in many regions, but consistent 200 qps sustained is where Dedicated reserved pools shine because you get guaranteed capacity and autoscale policies.
[00:02:38] Jamal Peters: What about batching? Won't batching increase latency for small single-call scoring?
[00:02:42] Devon Park: Right — continuous batching optimizes throughput, but for strict latency SLOs we configure smaller max batch windows and prefer dedicated nodes with high frequency scheduling. We also have adaptive batching and prefix/KV cache which reduces token compute for repeated contexts.
[00:02:56] Maya Ortiz: What's the cost delta we should expect between hosted and dedicated for your 200 qps burst scenario? Can you ballpark?
[00:03:03] Devon Park: Ballpark is tricky without exact prompt lengths and token rates; generally dedicated lowers per-token compute cost because of reserved GPUs and tighter packing. For example, a hosted path might be 1.5–2x per-token cost at similar latency. We'll send a sizing worksheet so you can plug your traffic and prompts to get a clearer number.
[00:03:18] Leila Chen: Okay, that's useful. Can you also show us the model variants? We use some open models today, and want to know if Redwood supports their quantized variants and the impact on quality.
[00:03:27] Devon Park: Yep — we maintain a catalog of vetted open models, plus quantization profiles. For most workloads, 8-bit quant gives major cost savings and small quality delta. We surface regression tests tied to prompt sets as part of Redwood Optimize — we can run an eval on your prompts to quantify delta.
[00:03:43] Maya Ortiz: Great. On compliance notes — we need SSAE/SOC2 docs and a data processing agreement. Also, is there an audit log we can pull for user activity and calls?
[00:03:54] Sara Lin: Yes to DPA and SOC2. Audit logs are available with the enterprise package and for Private deployments we provide full control plane logs in your VPC. We'll attach the SOC2 PDF and a short security FAQ link.
[00:04:06] Jamal Peters: About networking: for VPC peering, do you require static IP ranges? How do you handle ingress?
[00:04:12] Devon Park: For Private (VPC) we support VPC peering, private link in supported clouds, or on-prem via an appliance. We typically ask for a CIDR for routing and provide a small set of egress endpoints for control plane callbacks. We'll share the network checklist.
[00:04:25] Leila Chen: If we do a hosted pilot and later move to Dedicated or Private, how smooth is model/versioning and rollout?
[00:04:31] Devon Park: The API is consistent across modes. You pin model versions and rollout policies independent of infra. We support canary deployments and automatic fallback policies so you can gracefully fail to a cheaper variant if a node is saturated.
[00:04:43] Maya Ortiz: Do you have rate limits that could block our UX during spikes? We have bursty user behavior during sign-ups.
[00:04:48] Sara Lin: Hosted has tiered rate limits; we can increase for pilots. Dedicated gets you higher limits and predictable throughput. Also, routing policies can divert low-priority requests to cheaper regions or model variants.
[00:05:01] Jamal Peters: For the pilot we want to measure both quality and cost. What's the suggested experiment?
[00:05:06] Devon Park: Suggestion: start hosted with the 50k credit, run your prompt set and production-like traffic for 7–14 days, capture p95 latency, token burn, and error rate. We'll run the same workload on a recommended dedicated config in our test harness to show cost vs latency differences. That gives you apples-to-apples.
[00:05:21] Leila Chen: How do we provision route-level RBAC so only certain engineers can call production models?
[00:05:25] Devon Park: We support API key scoping and route-level permissions in the Console. For enterprise, tie into SSO and enforce SCIM provisioning.
[00:05:34] Maya Ortiz: Any gotchas around KV cache or prefix caching when we use multi-tenant data?
[00:05:39] Devon Park: You can scope caches per-tenant; for privacy you should avoid sharing KV across tenants. We also recommend TTLs and an eviction policy for sensitive prompts.
[00:05:49] Jamal Peters: Ok. On the timeline — if we want a dedicated pilot in four weeks, what are realistic milestones?
[00:05:55] Sara Lin: Week 0: sign PO + pilot contract. Week 1: set up dedicated pool or reserved nodes, networking handoff. Week 2: ingest prompt set, run baseline benchmarks, iterate on config. Week 3–4: production-like traffic test and evaluation, handoff. We can compress some steps depending on approvals.
[00:06:12] Maya Ortiz: That seems reasonable. Can you estimate contract lead time for privacy addendums?
[00:06:16] Sara Lin: Depends on legal cycles — typical 1–3 weeks for standard DPA and security addenda, faster if security team is aligned. We'll surface templates.
[00:06:25] Leila Chen: On technical deep dive next week — can Devon walk our infra folks through the network checklist and a traffic simulation?
[00:06:31] Devon Park: Absolutely. I'd like to see your 7-day histogram of traffic and a prompt sample beforehand. That helps me pick the right GPU family and quantization profile.
[00:06:40] Jamal Peters: We'll get that over. One more question — how do you handle drift and model updates? If you pin a version, can we opt into auto-updates?
[00:06:46] Devon Park: You can pin or enable automatic rollouts. We also provide quality regression alerts tied to prompt sets; Redwood Optimize can run continuous evals and alert if a new model causes degradation.
[00:06:58] Maya Ortiz: I think that's a solid high-level view. A few small follow-ups: can you provide an example pricing comparison for our 200 qps burst scenario and a link to the SOC2?
[00:07:08] Sara Lin: I'll send the pricing worksheet and SOC2 link after this call. Devon will attach the benchmark sheet.
[00:07:13] Leila Chen: Thanks. Also, does Redwood support function/tool calling or streaming for our chat flows?
[00:07:18] Devon Park: Yes, streaming and tool calling are supported. For chat flows we recommend streaming to reduce perceived latency; function calling depends on your orchestration but we provide structured output support.
[00:07:30] Jamal Peters: Any limits on model context window? We often have longer documents for retrieval augmented generation.
[00:07:35] Devon Park: We support a range of context lengths; for very long contexts we recommend chunking and retrieval + KV cache to keep costs down. Some high-context model variants are more expensive — we'll recommend a fit for your RAG pattern.
[00:07:48] Maya Ortiz: Ok, last thing — will you include a short HOWTO for time-to-first-token for our engineers? We want to reduce friction.
[00:07:54] Sara Lin: Yes — we'll include a step-by-step quickstart: sign up, SDK snippet, send sample prompt, and validate response. That usually gets engineers running in under 30 minutes.
[00:08:03] Leila Chen: Perfect.
[00:08:06] Sara Lin: Cool. Let's do the recap and owners.
[00:08:09] [recap segment — slightly auto-generated] Sara Lin: Recap — Redwood will: send SOC2 and security docs, send pricing and pilot paperwork, provide 50k token hosted pilot credit, SE will share benchmark/sizing worksheet, and schedule a follow-up deep dive for VPC/networking. BlueHarbor will send prompt set and traffic hist.
[00:08:35] Maya Ortiz: Sounds good. Thanks everyone.
[00:08:37] Jamal Peters: Thanks.
[00:08:38] Devon Park: Thanks all, I'll follow up with the worksheet.
[00:08:42] Sara Lin: End.

Notes/links mentioned: Security FAQ (link to SOC2 PDF) — (sent post-call), Benchmark worksheet (Devon to attach), Pilot contract template (Sara to attach).
